description: **Seat roster** — Amore sessions register in a house-neutral presence directory (`~/.house/coord/presence/`) at start and drop the entry on exit. New houses stamped by `amore init` emit Peers and Origin at session start (the model sees them as a system-reminder). The welcome splash and the iris Dashboard Pulse show the same live roster, so two sessions on one seat can name each other.

**Also** — in-process `/minimal` and `/fullscreen`, plugin marketplace CTAs, feedback image attachments, MCP elicitation, workflow remote-bundle load plus `agent_budget`, Ctrl+S prompt stash, and a concurrent subagent sampling gate. `xai-grok-version` tracks upstream 1.0.8.

**No more console windows flashing on Windows** — the iris daemon spawned its qmd runtime probes without a hidden window, so every status check, search and index refresh flashed a `node.exe` console on the desktop. The probes are hidden now, and the fleet updater relaunches daemons with a hidden console of their own instead of none.

**Hotfix tags** — release tags track the upstream pin (`v1.0.6` is upstream 1.0.6 plus the fork's delta); a fix cut between two pins is `v1.0.6-hotfix.1`, which `amore update` orders after `v1.0.6` and before `v1.0.7`. Fleets on this release or later are offered hotfixes.
**Startup-failure advice names your binary** — the "try a larger startup budget" and "stop the shared leader" commands on the startup-failure screen say `amore`, not `grok`.

**Status line** — a configurable status line under the prompt: model, cost, context use, session name, and custom command segments that re-run on a timer (`refresh_interval`). See `docs/user-guide/25-status-line.md`.
**Permissions** — tool approvals are remembered by default, and "Never allow" is persistent for MCP tools and web-fetch domains.

**Also** — compact on a model-family switch, identical tool-call loops are interrupted earlier (two tiers), paused workflows stay visible, e-mail addresses render as `mailto:` links, and `GROK_CONNECT_UI_TIMEOUT_SECS` raises the startup connect budget.

**House compact packet** — after compact, the successor sees the house orientation packet (re-read current-state and the active task; the summary is forensics). The summarizer receives the PreCompact snapshot through `/compact keep`, alongside any keep-line you already passed.
**Selection** — drag-copy in scrollback is more reliable, `/session-info` rows copy on drag, and Text selection can be set to `word_select` for double-click word / triple-click paragraph.

**Worktree GC** — idle copies under the house worktrees dir are reclaimed when safe, and never when they hold the last copy of the work. `amore worktree gc --max-age 7d` is the manual pass (`--dry-run` first).
**Arabic and Persian** — optional RTL reordering in scrollback. Turn on in `/settings`, or `[scrollback.display] rtl_bidi = true`. Off by default.
**Hooks can rewrite a tool call** — a `PreToolUse` hook may return `updatedInput` to replace the model's arguments before the tool runs.

**House compact hook** — `amore init` plants a PreCompact / PostCompact hook that emits a disk-orientation packet (re-read current-state and the active task; the summary is forensics). The harness does not yet inject that packet into the successor conversation.

**Dream proposals no longer double-write** — Lucerna materializes ### Proposal: blocks after the agent finishes. The agent is told not to write forge/proposals/ itself, and a second file with the same title (even under a shorter slug) is skipped.

**The Lucerna tab shows the charter cap you just wrote** — iris overlays .amore/lucerna/budgets.json onto a stale state.json snapshot, so raising the token ceiling is visible immediately. A running Lucerna adopts the file on the next idle poll (not mid-dream). Million-scale caps render as 2M, not 2000K.

**Auto-commit can be turned off** — a on the Lucerna tab cycles off / dry-run / live. Dry-run still drafts (and spends tokens); off does not. iris lucerna enable auto-commit off|dry-run|live writes autoCommitEnabled on enable.json. auto-commit-live on|off still means live vs dry-run and keeps drafting on.

**Lucerna's Budgets panel tells the truth it already promised** — the Running tab now shows live caps, capability (ready / cooling / refusing), and provenance (source, aboveShipped). This honours a published claim; it is not a new spend surface.

**Enablement and other charter edits apply at the next cycle** — deleting or flipping enable.json, budgets.json, or chores.json stops the next cycle from starting. The halt sentinel and process stop are the only paths that interrupt work already running.

**Charter files are no longer daemon-writable** — an autonomous maintenance dream could write the file that enables autonomous maintenance dreams; it now cannot. No exploitation is known — the boundary was simply drawn in the wrong place. Charter lives under <house>/.amore/lucerna/; runtime stays under instruments/lucerna/.

**Operator knobs: budgets.json / chores.json** — six spend scalars and a narrowing chore roster, house-local, b / c on the Lucerna tab, iris lucerna budgets / chores on the CLI. The file may raise a cap above shipped (aboveShipped is visible). The roster cannot invent a key or name a spawn flag. Confirm dialogs and the JSON content-type check are not authentication; iris stays loopback-unauthenticated. A planner reservation refuses starting a call when remaining room is too small — it does not make overspend impossible. Dreams-off is not spend-off: drafting still spends until auto-commit itself is off.

**Lucerna status tells the truth** — iris honors the daemon's adaptive `intervalMs` for staleness, checks process liveness (a dead daemon reads Stopped; start/stop stop guessing), and the Activity card shows **Running** with the live phase; activity and last actions render from the fields the daemon writes.

**Lucerna stays visibly alive during long work** — auto-commit and dream cycles advertise a bounded work-in-progress window and refresh the heartbeat while they run; a graceful stop leaves an honest stopped tombstone.
**Horizon theme** — the pager gains the iris app's default palette as a selectable theme (`/theme horizon`): a rose brand accent with green success and cyan information on the dark `#1c1e26` ground.

**Amore Build 1.0** — the Sessions member lands at full depth: a microscope that navigates the whole corpus with turn-level detail, scoped probes with trends, a map drawing real resume and shared-artifact links, and generated session titles.

**`amore update`, end to end** — a default-on kill-switchable check surfaces a welcome tip; Ctrl+U or `amore update` applies a verified fleet transaction moving amore and every installed companion together, with `--rollback` and doctor fleet coherence. Never unattended.

**Hardening** — the update origin is single-sourced and gate-pinned to this repository's releases; workflow actions are SHA-pinned; released assets prove their own update surface on all five targets; a remote config response can no longer block startup.

**Agent turns are more reliable** — a delta carrying more than one reasoning-trace spelling no longer ends the turn; a zero-output length stop is treated as input overflow and routes to compaction; foreign reasoning signatures are stripped on a model-backend switch.
**Scheduled and background work survives a disconnect** — a session holding scheduled tasks or running background work is no longer evicted as idle, so an agent-created obligation is not destroyed.

**Leader control tolerates mixed protocol versions** — control now enforces a per-command minimum floor instead of exact equality, so a future protocol bump is a soft tolerance rather than a fleet-wide cutover.
**Failures are traceable** — an unknown model's context window warns and surfaces once instead of a silent over-large default; the provider request-id is captured and logged on every failed response.

**Cost and config hardening** — cache-write tokens are counted; an out-of-list reasoning effort clamps to the nearest declared option; action chord collisions are reported instead of silently first-winning.
**Rendering is grapheme-aware** — width and truncate no longer cut flags or emoji families mid-glyph.
**Release hygiene** — the unenforced allowed_tools skill field is removed; the iris TUI dependencies are pinned to named floors; CI now smokes both canonical installers.

**The house keeps itself** — Lucerna's agentic maintenance dreams run governed sessions through your own model configuration and write reviewable reports and proposals; opt-in install, dreams off by default, budgets, wall-clock kill, default-deny writes.

**Semantic search sets itself up** — `amore init` runs `iris qmd setup`: pinned runtime, house collections, full hybrid search by default, and the iris daemon keeps the index fresh automatically; `--no-qmd` opts out.
**The review loop closes in the dash** — dreams and proposals list pending-first with a full reading overlay, and review flips land byte-exact from the TUI or the CLI.

**The typed-edge graph gains agentic tiers** — `iris edges update --tier 2` generates and judges edges through a headless `amore` spawn with a quote-validity gate; every edge carries tier and provenance, stewardship stays after the fact.
**Iris moves home** — client state now lives at `~/.amore/instruments/iris/`; a legacy `~/.iris` migrates automatically on first run (verified, marked, never deleted).
**Doctor covers the companions** — an instruments section reports iris / lucerna / speculum presence, versions, honest enablement, and the managed search stack.
**Init refuses to nest houses** — bare `amore init` inside an existing house is refused; `amore init .` adopts a pre-manifest house without overwriting your files.

**Opt-in companions ride the same release tag** — `amore init --with-lucerna` and `amore init --with-speculum` fetch the house steward and session mirror from the matching GitHub Release (sha256-verified, linked beside `amore`); both default off, iris stays default-on with `--no-iris`.

**The system prompt introduces the harness by its right name** — the compiled-in prompt templates lagged their plaintext sources by one commit, leaving a stale product name and docs path in the resident model's system prompt; regenerated, with the regeneration script now shipping in-tree.

**Linux glibc floor lowered to 2.35** — release lanes build on Ubuntu 22.04 runners so binaries run on Ubuntu 22.04+/Debian 12+; the installers now smoke-test the installed binary (must run and print a version) and restore the rollback copy on failure.

**The crowned heart** — the welcome mark is now a gold three-point crown resting on a rose heart, taken from the site's own art and rasterized in braille; both tiers regenerate from `scripts/gen_amore.py`, same shine sweep.

**Iris lands on PATH with the house** — `amore init` links the companion beside the `amore` binary (no manual PATH step), and the planted `AGENTS.md` wires the resident agent to the iris org verbs and `iris regula lint`.

**DeepSeek V4 Flash is the recommended model path** — the wizard's first slot writes `deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash-0731` over OpenRouter; GLM-5.2 recipes remain, and the setup docs are model-agnostic (`docs/setup-models.md`).
**Iris installs with the house** — `amore init` downloads the companion by default (`--no-iris` opts out), and the iris daemon now binds loopback only.
**Install one-liners** — installer scripts fetch the newest release asset for your platform, verify its sha256, and keep a rollback of any previous install.
